title: Signal Shift
premise: A fast neon sci-fi match-3 score attack where the player swaps adjacent signal tiles to form matches, trigger cascades, and build score before a 60-second uplink window closes.
interaction_model: Single-screen touch or mouse input; tap one tile then an adjacent tile, or drag between adjacent tiles to swap. Tap after game over to restart.
objective: Score as many points as possible within 60 seconds by creating valid 3-or-more matches and chaining cascades.
progression: Short arcade runs with immediate restart, rising score pressure, and combo-based payoff rather than level unlocking or narrative progression.
theme: Cyber arcade signal-routing fantasy with glowing grid panels, techno mascots, holographic overlays, and reactive streaming-style feedback.
mood: Energetic, playful, flashy, and slightly futuristic with satisfying combo spectacle.
likely_audience: fans of timed match-3 score attack games
players who enjoy flashy audiovisual feedback
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is primarily a timed match-3 puzzle game.
High confidence that score attack and combo cascades are the core progression loop.
Moderate confidence that the signal/uplink fiction is mostly aesthetic wrapper rather than deep mechanical theme.
Low confidence for any meta progression, unlocks, or multiple modes because none are present in the inspected code.
recreation_prompt: Recreate a polished single-screen browser game called "Signal Shift," a mobile-friendly neon sci-fi match-3 score attack played on a 6-column by 8-row grid. The player swaps only orthogonally adjacent tiles, either by tapping one tile and then a neighbor or by dragging into a neighbor, and every valid move must create a horizontal or vertical match of 3 or more identical tiles or it snaps back as a failed move. Use six distinct glowing tile types with emoji-like futuristic identities such as robot, alien glitch, satellite, battery, crystal, and spark, each rendered as glossy luminous chips on a dark holographic board. The session should last 60 seconds, with a top HUD showing score framed as SIGNAL and a countdown framed as UPLINK. Clearing matches should remove tiles with a quick fade-and-shrink animation, collapse columns downward, spawn new tiles from above, and continue resolving cascades automatically for combo chains. Score should reward longer matches more heavily, with 4-matches and 5-plus matches gaining multipliers, and chain reactions adding an additional bonus multiplier. Presentation should feel juicy and arcade-like: glowing board frame, animated tile pulses, toast notifications for points and combos, floating danmaku praise text for bigger chains, combo and fail reaction GIF moments, and responsive audio with ambient arcade background, swap clicks, collect sounds, combo stingers, fail sounds, and game-over feedback. On timeout, dim the board and show a game-over overlay such as "Signal Lost" with final score and a prompt to tap to restart immediately. Keep the game focused on replayable score chasing rather than levels, inventory, or story, and make it feel smooth, readable, and satisfying on both desktop and touch devices.
